verses.pali: เอวัมเม สุตัง, เอกัง สะมะยัง ภะคะวา, สาวัตถิยัง วิหะระติ, เชตะวะเน อะนาถะปิณฑิกัสสะ อาราเม, ตัต๎ระ โข ภะคะวา ภิกขู อามันเตสิ ภิกขะโวติ, ภะทันเตติ เต ภิกขู ภะคะวะโต ปัจจัสโสสุง, ภะคะวา เอตะทะโวจะ.
verses.pali_roman: evamme sutaṃ, ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā, sāvatthiyaṃ viharati, jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme, tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi bhikkhavoti, bhadanteti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ, bhagavā etadavoca.
verses.english: Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Savatthi, in Jeta's Grove, Anathapindika's park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: 'Bhikkhus.' 'Venerable sir,' those bhikkhus replied. The Blessed One said this:

verses.pali: ทะสะ อิเม ภิกขะเว ธัมมา ปัพพะชิเตนะ อะภิณ๎หัง ปัจจะเวกขิตัพพา. กะตะเม ทะสะ.
verses.pali_roman: dasa ime bhikkhave dhammā pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbā. katame dasa.
verses.english: There are these ten things, bhikkhus, that one who has gone forth should reflect on again and again. What ten?

verses.pali: เววัณณิยัมหิ อัชฌูปะคะโตติ ปัพพะชิเตนะ อะภิณ๎หัง ปัจจะเวกขิตัพพัง.
verses.english: 'I have come to a state of being without caste': this should be reflected on again and again by one who has gone forth.

verses.pali: ปะระปะฏิพัทธา เม ชีวิกาติ ปัพพะชิเตนะ อะภิณ๎หัง ปัจจะเวกขิตัพพัง.
verses.pali_roman: parapaṭibaddhā me jīvikāti pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ.
verses.english: 'My life is dependent on others': this should be reflected on again and again by one who has gone forth.

verses.pali: อัญโญ เม อากัปโป กะระณีโยติ ปัพพะชิเตนะ อะภิณ๎หัง ปัจจะเวกขิตัพพัง.
verses.pali_roman: añño me ākappo karaṇīyoti pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ.
verses.english: 'My bearing should be other than it was': this should be reflected on again and again by one who has gone forth.

verses.pali: กัจจิ นุ โข เม อัตตา สีละโต นะ อุปะวะทะตีติ ปัพพะชิเตนะ อะภิณ๎หัง ปัจจะเวกขิตัพพัง.
verses.pali_roman: kacci nu kho me attā sīlato na upavadatīti pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ.
verses.english: 'Does my own conscience reproach me as to virtue?': this should be reflected on again and again by one who has gone forth.

verses.pali: กัจจิ นุ โข มัง อะนุวิจจะ วิญญู สะพ์รัห์มะจารี สีละโต นะ อุปะวะทันตีติ ปัพพะชิเตนะ อะภิณ๎หัง ปัจจะเวกขิตัพพัง.
verses.pali_roman: kacci nu kho maṃ anuvicca viññū sabrahmacārī sīlato na upavadantīti pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ.
verses.english: 'Do my wise companions in the holy life, having examined me, reproach me as to virtue?': this should be reflected on again and again by one who has gone forth.

verses.pali: สัพเพหิ เม ปิเยหิ มะนาเปหิ นานาภาโว วินาภาโวติ, ปัพพะชิเตนะ อะภิณ๎หัง ปัจจะเวกขิตัพพัง.
verses.pali_roman: sabbehi me piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvoti, pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ.
verses.english: 'There is a parting and a separation from all that is dear and pleasing to me': this should be reflected on again and again by one who has gone forth.

verses.pali: กัมมัสสะโกมหิ กัมมะทายาโท กัมมะโยนิ กัมมะพันธุ กัมมะปะฏิสะระโณ, ยัง กัมมัง กะริสสามิ กัล๎ยาณัง วา ปาปะกัง วา, ตัสสะ ทายาโท ภะวิสสามีติ, ปัพพะชิเตนะ อะภิณ๎หัง ปัจจะเวกขิตัพพัง.
verses.pali_roman: kammassakomhi kammadāyādo kammayoni kammabandhu kammapaṭisaraṇo, yaṃ kammaṃ karissāmi kalyāṇaṃ vā pāpakaṃ vā, tassa dāyādo bhavissāmīti, pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ.
verses.english: 'I am the owner of my kamma, heir to my kamma, born of my kamma, kindred to my kamma, abide supported by my kamma; whatever kamma I shall do, good or bad, of that I shall be the heir': this should be reflected on again and again by one who has gone forth.

verses.pali: กะถัมภูตัสสะ เม รัตตินทิวา วีติปะตันตีติ ปัพพะชิเตนะ อะภิณ๎หัง ปัจจะเวกขิตัพพัง.
verses.pali_roman: kathaṃbhūtassa me rattindivā vītipatantīti pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ.
verses.english: 'How do the days and nights pass for me?': this should be reflected on again and again by one who has gone forth.

checks.issue: NUMBERING OFFSET, worth a decision. The book numbers the ten reflections 1-10, but the sutta opens with two unnumbered lines — the nidana and 'katame dasa' — which are chanted and so must be verses. That makes the book's item 1 into verse 3, and every item is offset by two. Book view hides verse numbers so nothing shows there, but the verse-by-verse study view prints them and they will not match the page. The same offset will hit every numbered list that follows a preamble.

FIRST CHANT WITH A BOOK NUMBER. The book prints '1.' before the title, so book_number is 1. This is the book's own chant numbering, not a page number and not a verse number, and it has not been derived by counting.

WORDS REJOINED ACROSS HYPHENS, two of them. Item 3 breaks ปัจจะเวกขิตัพพัง as 'ปัจจะเวก-' / 'ขิตัพพัง', and item 7 breaks กัมมะปะฏิสะระโณ as 'กัมมะปะฏิ-' / 'สะระโณ'. Both hyphens are justification, not spelling, so both words are recorded whole.
The nidana is the standard Savatthi opening. Reproduced as printed, including ตัต๎ระ with the yamakkan and the commas the book sets, rather than normalised to a standard edition's punctuation.
CONTINUES. Reflections 9 and 10 are on page 20 and have not been written from memory of the canon.

vocabulary.meaning: one gone forth — a monastic, as distinct from a householder
again and again, constantly — the point of the discourse is repetition, not a single reflection

vocabulary.pali: ปัจจะเวกขิตัพพัง
vocabulary.meaning: should be reflected upon, reviewed — looking back over one's own condition
difference of appearance, loss of caste — the shaven head and ochre robe that set a monastic outside the ordinary social order

vocabulary.pali: สะพ์รัห์มะจารี
vocabulary.meaning: a companion in the holy life — a fellow monastic, one who lives the same brahmacariya

vocabulary.pali: กัมมัสสะโก
vocabulary.meaning: owner of one's kamma — the first of the five phrases in reflection 7, which together are chanted daily
heir — one who inherits, here of one's own actions

vocabulary.pali: รัตตินทิวา
vocabulary.meaning: nights and days — the pair taken together as the passing of time

batch_status.notes: A NEW DIVISION of the book opens here: พระสูตร ปาฐะ และคาถา, the suttas and passages appointed for morning chanting. Pages 1-18 were the services themselves; this is the material chanted within them. It also brings the first printed CHANT NUMBER — '1.' before the title — so book_number is populated for the first time and later pages should be watched for 2., 3. and so on. The numbering-offset check on verse 3 is the one worth a decision: a numbered list preceded by unnumbered chanted lines cannot keep the book's item numbers as its verse numbers, and this will recur.
